drug_class: Opioid analgesic combination (narcotic pain reliever plus non-narcotic pain reliever)
purpose: This medicine is used to treat moderate to severe pain that other pain relievers have not been able to control well. It combines two different pain fighters in one pill to give you better relief. Your doctor may prescribe it after surgery, an injury, or for other painful conditions.
how_it_works: Oxycodone is an opioid that works by attaching to special receptors in your brain and spinal cord, which blocks pain signals and helps you feel more comfortable. Acetaminophen (the same ingredient in Tylenol) works in a different way to further reduce pain and can also lower a fever. Together, they work as a team to give you stronger pain relief than either one could alone.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or feeling sleepy, dizziness, constipation, nausea or upset stomach, vomiting, headache, and dry mouth are the most common side effects. Most people feel a little tired or lightheaded, especially when they first start taking it.
warnings: This medicine is a controlled substance and can be habit-forming, so take it exactly as your doctor prescribed and never share it with anyone else. Do NOT drink alcohol while taking this medication — it can cause dangerous or even life-threatening side effects. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Because it contains acetaminophen, avoid taking any other products that also contain acetaminophen (like Tylenol or many cold medicines) to prevent liver damage. Tell your doctor right away if you feel very sleepy, have slow or shallow breathing, or feel faint — these can be signs of a serious problem. Opioids can cause severe constipation, so drink plenty of water and ask your pharmacist about a stool softener if needed.
typical_dosing: The typical adult dose is 1 to 2 tablets every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain, but your doctor will prescribe the dose that is right for you. Do not take more than your doctor tells you to, and do not take more than 4,000 mg of acetaminophen total in one day from all sources. Always follow your prescription label carefully.
